changes: Added policy version, evaluation logic version, effective date, outcomes, and runtime authorization metadata to policies.
Split the multi-issue Cloud SQL record into separate backup and TLS findings, with aligned policy categories.
Added explicit Cloud SQL TLS and Cloud Functions ingress policies to remove category/resource-type mismatches.
Removed the clean compliant evaluation from findings and retained it as a resource-level compliance evaluation record.
Added remediation templates for all finding categories, including CMEK, backups, Workload Identity, key rotation, public ACLs, external IPs, TLS, and Cloud Functions ingress.
Replaced rollback plans that could restore public access or other noncompliant states with safe-stop / compliant-snapshot guidance.
Changed the catalog AUTO_EXECUTE default to REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL and made execution disabled by default; runtime authorization remains mandatory.
Added finding timestamps, status, evidence, confidence, policy version, remediation status, and normalized resource UID.
Added resource inventory/version metadata and reconciled violation IDs against actual findings.
Marked analytics-warehouse-export-prod as UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_RESCAN because its prior violation reference had no corresponding finding; did not falsely assert compliance.
Normalized every finding-level remediation decision to REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL and explicitly disabled execution by default.
safety_note: These are normalized seed-data examples. CLI commands, Terraform snippets, and tool names remain unvalidated examples and must not be executed directly in production. Runtime must independently enforce authorization, environment restrictions, approval, preconditions, dry-run/plan review, idempotency, post-change policy evaluation, health checks, and audit logging.
